prompts.name: food_berries
prompts.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Edit target: image 1 is an existing food sprite that MUST be fully redesigned; its big glossy red fruit and dark outline are rejected.
Authoritative style: image 2 is the actual original 128px mouse; image 3 is the approved early Soft Pixel game reference. Match the latter's stone, foliage and mouse rendering: subdued low-saturation colours, dusty warm values, soft fine square pixel clusters and broken coloured contours. Do not copy subjects or background of those style references.
Replace the entire food composition with a humble little gatherable mouse-food stash: THREE pale oat seeds and TWO SMALL dusty rose-red berries with tiny brown dots as the calyx, ONE small sage leaf. Seeds are dominant; berries smaller than the seeds. No giant donut-shaped caps. Low, loose, horizontal pile, side/slight three-quarter view. It belongs on the floor beside the original mouse.
Make it look hand painted AT A NATIVE 128x128 PIXEL ART SCALE, shown enlarged by nearest-neighbor. Clearly regular small square clusters make the contour and shading, like the supplied early reference. Gentle stepped shading, little mottled pixel patches, matte dry skin, not polished inventory icon. Keep restrained beige, oatmeal, muted red and sage colours with very low saturation, no white highlight spots, no bright orange, no shining fruit, no continuous black or chocolate outline, no coarse polygon shading, no smooth vector curves, no 3D bevel, no cast shadow.
Transparent background with real alpha. Entire object occupies 70% width, modest height, generous empty margin, no ground patch, scene, mouse, frame, labels or text. Readable as FOOD at 18 screen pixels, detailed but quiet at 54px. The original image's rendering is the problem: REDESIGN rather than pixelating the rejected illustration.

rejected_trials.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: in-world resource sprite, soft pixel game art for Dig Down.
Input images: Image 1 (berries) is the EDIT TARGET, preserve its identity as three edible berries with a leaf and a couple of seeds, but repaint it completely. Image 2 (existing mouse) and image 3 (early grassy field with mouse and stones) are the AUTHORITATIVE STYLE REFERENCES. Image 4 (old soil tile) is a supporting material/pixel-density reference. Do not draw any mouse, terrain square, grass field or scenery in the output.
Request: redraw only the berry food group in the exact understated soft-pixel/painterly-pixel language of the existing mouse and field references. This is a small practical prop belonging beside that mouse, not an inventory illustration.
Raster method: visibly authored square pixel clusters on a regular 128x128 logical pixel grid, then enlarged with nearest-neighbor for this output. Jagged stepped pixel contours, broken colored edges, small irregular pixel patches for soft volume, subtle 2-3 adjacent shades per color ramp. Pixel detail density comparable to the existing 128px mouse. No smooth vector curves, airbrushing or large polygon facets. No thick continuous chocolate outline. Matte cranberry/clay red berries with restrained muted warm highlights and a small sage olive leaf; pale oat seeds. Match the mouse reference's gentle warm contrast, light from upper left. Avoid saturated orange, white shiny spots, plastic gloss, heavy outlines, giant fruit calyxes, harsh low-poly facets, drop shadow, border, lettering.
Composition: one compact natural food pile, slight side/three-quarter game view, fills roughly 75% of square, ample transparent margins. Genuine alpha-transparent background, no floor or background color. Keep recognizable round fruit, leaf and seeds readable at 18 world pixels and 54 UI pixels. Return ONLY the new sprite.

Use case: background-extraction.
Edit target: supplied pixel art bundle of twigs and straw.
Remove the ENTIRE hazy brown glow surrounding the bundle and in all holes between stems. Preserve the actual pixel-art twigs, tie and straw, their shapes, muted colours, regular square pixel texture, position and relative scale. All pixels outside the physical material silhouettes MUST have alpha=0, including all blurred brown haze and shadows, with no semitransparent colored glow remaining. Clean discrete stepped pixel-art edges. No replacement background, shadow, aura, floor, border or text. Output one bundle on a genuinely transparent background. This is an alpha cutout cleanup, not a scene or lighting change.
